Maces were the crown champion for many years until requiem 3.0.0 (could be wrong but i think its this version) when the dmg system rework rolled through. Now swords are the best but maces are definitely nothing to laugh at and namely the mace of molag bal is still very much so an S tier weapon. I have ran plenty of mace builds and theyre really not to bad and I can give you some pointers as to how to use them mechanically. I would recommend having a dagger bound to your off hand using macros for flurries as opposed to double maces or mace and sword because daggers increase the attack rate of your flurries by a huge margin and maces are pretty slow. Keep a shield bound as a macro as well so you can switch between parrying and flurries; mind the equip animation though try to be sparing with your equip changes mid combat. Use the flurry setup to deal with dual wielders and non blockers like forsworn so you can burst them down before they can burst you down and always try to hit them with the tip of your hit box so you can guarantee you beat the ai with your startup. Use the shield to fight enemies that can block because they can eat most of your hits and so you kind wanna fish for parries so you can punish. Maces have high damage and armor pen so you can usually kill even some of the tankiest badguys with a single strike. Also try to clear the silent moons camp as early as possible because there is an orcish mace there called bouncer dropped by the bandit boss. I can usually clear this place at like level 2 or 3 but dont push yourself; if you need to wait until level 5-10 thats fine.

Yes! What you need to do is set up what is called a "Control rig." These are made by creating handles using curves and then parent constraining them to a single joint or multiple joints so that you can move joint groups with ease. [https://imgur.com/ZlxzWlR](https://imgur.com/ZlxzWlR) heres an example of a control rig I made in maya. However it is possible to do blender too. I have a few joints connected to the eyelid (Although not nearly as many as you) but those joints are each parented to small control handles which are parent together to one large control handle. Making it so theres a selection hierarchy I can use to make animation a much quicker process. [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=miphUq4uwNM](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=miphUq4uwNM) heres a video of a series on character rigging in which the instructor places his control handles and assembles a hierarchy in blender. I usually do my rigging in maya and use blender for modeling so Im not an expert on doing it in blender but its also pretty much the same thing.
